evidence.heroSub: We claim to have the most transparent adaptive learning engine in coding education. This page is the proof — or the failure to provide it. Every number here is reproducible from our open source code.
evidence.s1Lead: Whetzy runs a six-component adaptive stack. Every component is unit-tested. None of it is vendor-locked — the full implementation lives in

bkt.name: BKT
bkt.desc: HMM mastery estimation. Updates P(L) after every answer. 4-parameter model with explicit "I don't know" support.

fsrs.name: FSRS
fsrs.desc: Free Spaced Repetition Scheduler (SM-17 successor). Computes optimal review interval from stability and difficulty.

elo.name: Elo
elo.desc: Question difficulty calibration. Adjusts question ratings based on answer outcomes across all users.

bandit.name: Bandit (Thompson Sampling)
bandit.desc: Item selection in the adaptive placement test (BanditCAT). Live at /placement. Not connected to the main quiz loop — question selection there is handled directly by Elo.

dkt.name: DKT (LSTM)
dkt.desc: Deep Knowledge Tracing. LSTM trained on answer sequences; selects the next skill in a live A/B experiment. Not a P(L) signal — BKT remains the sole mastery estimate.

irt.name: IRT (2-PL)
irt.desc: Item Response Theory. 2-PL model live in the adaptive placement test (/placement). Estimates initial skill level (θ) and selects items by discriminating difficulty.

evidence.s2Lead: Default parameters from Wilson et al. (2016) and Corbett & Anderson (1995). Per-skill overrides are planned for F23 once ≥30 beta users provide enough observations per skill to fit P(L₀) and P(T) via EM.

pl0.desc: Prior probability of knowing a skill before any practice

pt.desc: Probability of learning after one correct opportunity

pg.desc: Probability of guessing correctly without knowing

masteryThreshold.desc: Minimum P(L) to unlock the next module

idkPrior.desc: P(knows | says DK) / P(unknown | says DK) — stronger negative evidence than a wrong answer

evidence.assistmentsNoteText: the canonical distribution page returns HTTP 200 but exposes no scriptable download URL, and every commonly-cited GitHub mirror we checked 404'd. Recorded as a gap in
evidence.assistmentsNoteEnd: rather than silently skipped or substituted with a look-alike dataset.
evidence.s3Lead: Run on <1>synthetic-5</1> (Piech et al. 2015, <2>Deep Knowledge Tracing</2>) — a fixed, third-party, citable dataset, so the "adaptive engine" claim is not graded by our own homework. 4 000 students, 5 concepts, 50 responses each. Temporal split by student (3 200 train / 800 test, no shuffling); within every sequence, predicting response <3>t</3> uses only responses 1…<3>t</3>−1 of that same student.
evidence.readNoteStrong: Read this before quoting the numbers.
evidence.readNoteText: Responses are keyed by <1>concept id</1> (0–4), not question id — the representation our production engine actually uses, but <1>not</1> the paper's setup. Handing the model ground-truth concept labels removes within-concept difficulty and makes the task strictly easier for <1>both</1> models, which is why both score above the paper's 0.75 / 0.62. These numbers must never be reported as beating Piech et al. The margin is what transfers, and ours (+0.031) is far smaller than the paper's (+0.13): a well-fit BKT is a strong baseline over only 5 concepts. The one defensible claim here is narrow — <1>on concept-level synthetic-5, our DKT beats our grid-fit BKT by about 0.03 AUC.</1> Nothing stronger.
evidence.s3Disclaimer: BKT baseline uses <1>app/services/engine/bkt.py</1> unchanged; parameters were grid-searched on the train split only (coarse grid, not full Baum-Welch — the production model has no EM). Full methodology, the exact fitted parameters, and the ASSISTments failure log live in <1>docs/ml/kt-benchmark.json</1>. Reproduce with <1>python -m app.ml.benchmark_kt</1>. Generated 2026-09-13.
evidence.s4Lead: Scored across six weighted dimensions (total {{max}} pts). Scores are our own judgement based on public feature lists and hands-on testing — not independently audited. URLs and dates are recorded so you can verify them yourself.

community.label: Community:
community.text: Zero users today (H.10). Forums, peer review, and leaderboards need people.

mobileNative.label: Mobile native:
mobileNative.text: PWA only. No App Store / Play Store listing yet (H.2/H.3).

benchmarkSynthetic.label: Benchmark is synthetic, not real learners:
benchmarkSynthetic.text: synthetic-5 is generated data. We have no AUC on a real classroom dataset, and none on our own users.

assistmentsEdnet.label: ASSISTments / EdNet:
assistmentsEdnet.text: not integrated — ASSISTments 2009 has no scriptable download; the failure log is in the benchmark JSON.

perSkillCalibration.label: Per-skill calibration:
perSkillCalibration.text: production BKT ships literature defaults with no EM fitting. The grid search exists only inside the benchmark script.

report.title: Mastery report
report.notFound: We couldn't find this report. Check the link.
report.noTracks: No progress in any track yet.
report.method: Mastery is estimated by Whetzy's engine (BKT) from your answers; a skill counts as mastered from 95%. This is a snapshot as of the date shown; it is not a certificate and does not replace any vendor's exam.

twoFactor.title: Two-step verification
twoFactor.scan: Scan this code with your authenticator app (Google Authenticator, 1Password, Authy…).
twoFactor.qrAlt: QR code for your authenticator app
twoFactor.manual: Can't scan it? Type this key into the app:
twoFactor.backupIntro: Keep these backup codes somewhere safe. Each one works once if you lose your phone; we won't show them again.
twoFactor.disableLabel: Code from the app or a backup code
twoFactor.enabledDone: Two-step verification is on. We'll ask for a code when you sign in.
twoFactor.badCode: That code isn't valid. Try the one the app shows now.
twoFactor.error: That didn't work. Please try again.
